copy.en:
How fast does light travel?

Light zooms at about 300,000 kilometres per second in a vacuum — that's the fastest anything in the whole universe can go!
copy.tl:
Gaano kabilis ang liwanag?

Gumagalaw ang liwanag nang halos 300,000 kilometro bawat segundo sa vacuum — iyan ang pinakamabilis na bagay sa buong uniberso!
copy.bis:
Unsa ka paspas ang suga?

Ang suga mobalhin og mga 300,000 kilometro matag segundo sa vacuum — mao kini ang pinakadasig nga bisan unsa sa tibuok uniberso!

copy.en: A distance of one light-year is equal to about 9.5 trillion kilometers!
copy.tl: Ang isang light-year ay katumbas ng mga 9.5 trilyong kilometro!
copy.bis: Ang usa ka light-year katumbas sa mga 9.5 ka trilyon ka kilometro!

copy.en: A light-year is how far light travels in one year—about 9.46 trillion kilometres! It measures vast space distances. Proxima Centauri, the nearest star to our Sun, is 4.2 light-years away.
copy.tl: Ang light-year ay ang distansya na nilalakbay ng ilaw sa isang taon—mga 9.46 trilyong kilometro! Ginagamit ito para sa malalayong distansya sa kalawakan. Ang Proxima Centauri, pinakamalapit na bituin sa Araw, ay 4.2 light-years ang layo.
copy.bis: Ang light-year mao ang distansya nga gilakbay sa suga sulod sa usa ka tuig—mga 9.46 trilyon ka kilometro! Gigamit kini para sa layo nga distansya sa kalawakan. Ang Proxima Centauri, pinaka-duol nga bituin sa Adlaw, 4.2 light-years ang kalayoan.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes lightning as a flow of electricity and gives a safety tip (avoid being tallest or holding metal touching ground). It shares vocabulary and a general safety theme but does not directly teach the competency's core content.

copy.tl: Ang kidlat ay malakas na daloy ng kuryente mula ulap papalupa! Iwasan ang pagiging daanan nito: huwag maging pinakamataas o humawak ng metal na nakadikit sa lupa.
copy.bis: Ang kilat usa ka kusog nga agos sa kuryente gikan sa panganod! Ayaw pagka sayon nga agianan: ayaw pagka labing taas o paghawid og metal nga moabot sa yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Spread out a little! This way, if lightning strikes, not everyone gets hurt at the same time.

assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a lightning safety tip but does not teach that electricity is a flow of electrons, nor does it address handling electricity. It only touches on a safety measure for a lightning situation, which is too far from the competency's core content.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how light and sound can be harmful to people and make suggestions on how to protect oneself from them

copy.en:
What should a group do if caught outside in a lightning storm with no shelter?

Spread out a little! This way, if lightning strikes, not everyone gets hurt at the same time.
copy.tl:
Ano ang dapat gawin ng grupo kung naabutan ng kidlat sa labas na walang silungan?

Maghiwa-hiwalay nang kaunti! Para kung may tumama, hindi lahat masaktan nang sabay-sabay.
copy.bis:
Unsay buhaton sa grupo kung maabtan sa kilat sa gawas nga walay silonganan?

Magbulag-bulag og gamay! Aron kung naay moigo, dili tanan masakitan nga dungan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: crouch down low! Do not stand tall or be the tallest object around.

assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a lightning safety tip (crouching to avoid being struck). It does not teach that electricity is a flow of electrons, nor does it address safe measures in handling electricity (e.g., appliances, wiring). Lightning is a natural electrical discharge, not 'handling electricity,' so the card only shares the broad topic of electrical safety.

copy.en: If lightning catches you in an open area, crouch down low! Do not stand tall or be the tallest object around.
copy.tl: Kung naabutan ka ng kidlat sa malawak na lugar, yumuko ka! Huwag tumayo nang paitaas o maging pinakamataas sa paligid.
copy.bis: Kung maabtan ka sa kilat sa hawan nga dapit, yukbo ka! Ayaw pagbarog ug ayaw himoa ang imong kaugalingon nga pinakahataas.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions chlorophyll's role in photosynthesis but does not describe the process, raw materials, or products of photosynthesis or respiration. It only provides a related fact about nitrogen's role in making chlorophyll.

copy.en:
Why do plants need nitrogen?

Plants use nitrogen to make proteins and chlorophyll, the green stuff that helps them turn sunlight into food. Without it, they turn pale and stay small — that's why lightning's help in providing nitrogen matters!
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan ng halaman ang nitrogen?

Ginagamit ito ng halaman para gumawa ng protina at chlorophyll, ang berdeng bahagi na tumutulong gumawa ng pagkain mula sa araw. Kung kulang dito, namumutla at nananatiling maliit ang halaman — kaya mahalaga ang tulong ng kidlat sa pagbibigay nito!
copy.bis:
Nganong kinahanglan sa tanom ang nitrogen?

Gamiton sa tanom aron makahimo og protina ug chlorophyll, ang berde nga bahin nga motabang sa paghimo og pagkaon gikan sa adlaw. Kon kulang, mangluspad ug magpabilin nga gamay — mao nga importante ang tabang sa kilat!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because light travels much faster than sound!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card compares the speeds of light and sound but does not define speed as distance per time, which is the core of G4-F-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because light travels much faster than sound!

copy.en:
Why do we see lightning before hearing thunder?

Because light travels much faster than sound! The bright flash reaches our eyes first, so the rumble of thunder reaches our ears later.
copy.tl:
Bakit nakikita muna natin ang kidlat bago marinig ang kulog?

Dahil ang liwanag ay naglalakbay nang mas mabilis kaysa tunog! Ang liwanag ay una nang dumadating, kaya mas matagal dumating sa tainga natin ang ugong ng kulog.
copy.bis:
Nganong makita nato ang kidlat una madungog ang dalugdog?

Tungod kay ang kahayag mas paspas molakaw kaysa tingog! Ang kahayag una moabot, mao nga mas dugay moabot sa atong dalunggan ang dahunog sa dalugdog.

copy.en:
Does lightning really fall from the sky?

Surprise! The brightest part of lightning actually shoots upward from the ground to the cloud in less than a blink — that's why the whole bolt seems to flash at once!
copy.tl:
Mukhang nahuhulog ba ang kidlat mula sa ulap?

Gulat! Ang pinakamaliwanag na bahagi ng kidlat ay sumasabog pataas mula sa lupa patungong ulap sa loob ng kaunti pa sa isang kisapmata — kaya biglang sumiklab ang buong daanan!
copy.bis:
Morag nahulog ba ang kilat gikan sa panganod?

Gulat! Ang labing hayag nga bahin sa kilat misaka gikan sa yuta padulong sa panganod sa dili pa molabaw sa usa ka pamilok — busa kalit nga misiga ang tibuok agianan!

Who was Clara Lim-Sylianco?

Clara Lim-Sylianco was a Filipino scientist in the field of chemistry!

Sino si Clara Lim-Sylianco?

Si Clara Lim-Sylianco ay isang Pilipinong siyentista sa larangan ng chemistry!
copy.bis:
Kinsa si Clara Lim-Sylianco?

Si Clara Lim-Sylianco usa ka Pilipinong siyentista sa chemistry!

What do limestone rocks and seashells have in common?

They are both made mostly of calcium carbonate! It is the exact same chemical that makes up seashells and snail shells.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakapareho ng mga batong limestone at mga kabibe?

Pareho silang halos puro calcium carbonate! Ito ang parehong kemikal na bumubuo sa mga kabibe at bahay-kuhol.
copy.bis:
Unsay pagkapareho sa mga bato nga limestone ug mga kabibe?

Pareho silang halos puro calcium carbonate! Kini ang samang kemikal nga naghimo sa mga kabibe ug kabhang.

How long does it take for thick limestone to form?

It takes millions of years! It forms as the remains of sea animals pile up layer upon layer.
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal bago mabuo ang makapal na limestone?

Inabot ng millions of years! Nabuo ito habang patung-patong na naipon ang remains ng sea animals.
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay ang paghimo sa baga nga limestone?

Milyon-milyon ka tuig! Naporma kini samtang nagsapaw-sapaw ang remains sa sea animals.

Why is it important for families in the Philippines to be prepared for earthquakes?

Active faults run near our cities, like the West Valley Fault in Metro Manila, so families must always be ready!

May mga active fault na malapit sa mga siyudad, gaya ng West Valley Fault sa Metro Manila, kaya dapat handa palagi!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga importante nga andam ang mga pamilya sa Pilipinas para sa mga linog?

Adunay active fault duol sa mga siyudad, sama sa West Valley Fault sa Metro Manila, busa kinahanglan kanunay andam!

Ang matibay na gusaling itinayo nang tama sa matatag na lupa ay mas hindi madaling gumuho!

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions blood and the liver, which relate to the circulatory and digestive/excretory systems, but it does not describe how any of the listed body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work in simple terms. It only gives a brief fact about the liver cleaning blood, not a description of a system's function.

copy.en:
How does your liver clean your blood?

All our blood passes through the liver, which removes poisons and waste and sends them out — like a filter working 24 hours a day!
copy.tl:
Paano nililinis ng atay ang dugo mo?

Dumadaan ang lahat ng dugo natin sa atay, na tumatanggal ng lason at basura at nagpapadala nito palabas — parang salaan na gumagana 24 oras!
copy.bis:
Giunsa paglimpyo sa atay ang imong dugo?

Moagi ang tanan natong dugo sa atay, nga mokuha sa mga hilo ug basura ug magpagawas niini — sama sa salaan nga naglihok 24 ka oras!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We can't feel the liver working, so it's called a silent organ.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the liver but does not describe how any of the listed body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. It only states that the liver is silent and that check-ups matter, which is not direct instruction on system function.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We can't feel the liver working, so it's called a silent organ.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, and it does not explain how body systems work together. It only gives a general fact about the liver, which is not direct support for the competency's required representation or content.

copy.en:
Why is the liver called a 'silent organ'?

We can't feel the liver working, so it's called a silent organ. It can have a problem for a long time before any pain is felt — regular check-ups matter!
copy.tl:
Bakit tinatawag na 'tahimik na organo' ang atay?

Hindi natin nararamdaman ang atay habang gumagana, kaya tinatawag itong tahimik na organo. Maaaring matagal nang may problema bago pa ito masakit — kaya mahalaga ang regular na check-up!
copy.bis:
Ngano gitawag nga 'hilom nga organo' ang atay?

Dili nato mabati ang atay samtang naglihok, mao nga gitawag kini nga hilom nga organo. Mahimong dugay nang naay problema una pa mabati ang kasakit — mao nga importante ang regular nga check-up!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the liver also stores vitamins and iron the body needs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about liver storage of vitamins and iron, but does not describe how any of the listed body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. The liver is an organ associated with the digestive system, but the card provides no explanation of system function, so it is only topically related.

copy.en: Besides sugar, the liver also stores vitamins and iron the body needs — that's why eating liver is nutritious, rich in iron for healthy blood.
copy.tl: Bukod sa asukal, nag-iipon din ang atay ng bitamina at iron na kailangan ng katawan — kaya masustansya ang pagkaing atay, mayaman ito sa iron para sa malusog na dugo.
copy.bis: Gawas sa asukal, ang atay nagtipig usab og mga bitamina ug iron nga gikinahanglan sa lawas — mao nga masustansya ang pagkaong atay, dato kini sa iron alang sa himsog nga dugo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The liver stores extra sugar from your food and releases it as energy whenever your body needs it.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a metabolic function of the liver (storing and releasing sugar as energy), not how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory system works. The liver is associated with the digestive system, but the card does not teach digestive-system functioning, so it is only related to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The liver stores extra sugar from your food and releases it as energy whenever your body needs it.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using a labeled diagram, trace how food travels through the digestive tract and explain how different digestive processes work, including mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, and elimination
assignedReviews.reason: G8-L-1 requires a labeled diagram tracing food through the digestive tract and explaining digestive processes (mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, elimination). The card only states that the liver stores and releases sugar as energy; it does not trace food through the digestive tract, use a labeled diagram, or address any listed digestive process. It is unrelated to the required content.

copy.en: The liver stores extra sugar from your food and releases it as energy whenever your body needs it.
copy.tl: Iniimbak ng atay ang sobrang asukal mula sa pagkain at inilalabas ito bilang enerhiya kapag kailangan.
copy.bis: Ang atay nagatipig sa sobra nga asukal gikan sa pagkaon ug gibuhi kini nga kusog kon gikinahanglan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A shark is a fish
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that a shark is a fish, which touches on animal classification, but it does not use a table, does not classify living things into the named groups, and provides no information about the characteristics used to group animals. It only states one fact about sharks, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: sharks have been around for so long, they're even older than dinosaurs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the geologic time scale helps to recount the history of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card notes that sharks are older than dinosaurs, which is a fact about Earth's history, but it does not explain the geologic time scale or how it recounts Earth's history. The statement is too vague and does not teach the competency's concept.

copy.en: A shark is a fish, but its skeleton is made of bendy cartilage instead of hard bone — and sharks have been around for so long, they're even older than dinosaurs.
copy.tl: Ang pating ay isang isda, pero ang kalansay nito ay gawa sa malambot na cartilage, hindi tigas na buto — matagal nang umiiral ang mga pating, mas matanda pa sila kaysa sa mga dinosaur.
copy.bis: Ang iho usa ka isda, apan ang kalansay niini hinimo sa humok nga cartilage, dili gahi nga bukog — dugay na kaayong nabuhi ang mga iho, mas karaan pa kay sa mga dinosaur.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: need oxygen to turn food into energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that animals need oxygen to turn food into energy. It does not describe the process of respiration or photosynthesis, nor does it identify the raw materials and products beyond a vague mention of oxygen and food. This is background knowledge, not direct instruction for the G8 competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: need oxygen to turn food into energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions breathing and oxygen but does not identify or describe the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work. It is only tangentially related to respiration.

copy.en:
Why can't we ever stop breathing?

Almost all animals, including people, need oxygen to turn food into energy — that's why we can never stop breathing!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi tayo puwedeng huminto sa paghinga?

Halos lahat ng hayop, kasama ang tao, ay nangangailangan ng oxygen para makakuha ng enerhiya mula sa pagkain — kaya hindi tayo makakahinto sa paghinga!
copy.bis:
Nganong dili ta puwede mohunong ug ginhawa?

Halos tanang hayop, lakip ang tawo, nagkinahanglan og oxygen aron makakuha og kusog gikan sa pagkaon — mao nga dili ta makahunong sa pagginhawa!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: scientists use its scientific name to make sure everyone means the same one
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the importance of the six-kingdom system and the three-domain system of classification of living things
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses scientific naming to avoid ambiguity, but does not address the six-kingdom or three-domain systems of classification or their importance.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One kind of animal can have different names in Tagalog, Bisaya, and Ilokano
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about local names and scientific names, not about using a table to classify living things into the named groups based on similar characteristics. The required table format is also absent.

copy.en: One kind of animal can have different names in Tagalog, Bisaya, and Ilokano, so scientists use its scientific name to make sure everyone means the same one.
copy.tl: Ang iisang uri ng hayop ay maaaring may ibang pangalan sa Tagalog, Bisaya, at Ilokano, kaya ginagamit ang pangalang siyentipiko para siguradong iisa ang tinutukoy.
copy.bis: Ang usa ka matang sa mananap mahimong adunay lainlaing ngalan sa Tagalog, Bisaya, ug Ilokano, mao nga gigamit ang ngalang siyentipiko aron sigurado nga usa ra ang gipasabot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A locust is a kind of grasshopper that gathers together into huge, moving swarms!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that a locust is a type of grasshopper, which touches on animal grouping but does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups (plants, animals, microorganisms) as required by the competency. No classification table or comparison of multiple groups is provided.

copy.en:
What is a locust?

A locust is a kind of grasshopper that gathers together into huge, moving swarms!
copy.tl:
Ano ang balang?

Ang balang ay isang uri ng tipaklong na nagtitipon sa napakalaking kuyog!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang balang?

Ang balang usa ka matang sa apan nga nagatapok sa dakong panon o langkay!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The longer a grain is tumbled by waves, the finer, rounder, and smoother it becomes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the physical rounding and smoothing of grains due to wave tumbling, which is an effect of abrasion/weathering. It does not demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials (e.g., movement from one place to another). The competency focuses on transport, while the card focuses on grain shape change, so it is only related to erosion.

copy.en: The longer a grain is tumbled by waves, the finer, rounder, and smoother it becomes!
copy.tl: Mas matagal na nahuhulma sa alon ang isang butil, mas pino, bilog, at makinis ito!
copy.bis: Kung mas dugay nga giligid sa balud ang usa ka lugas, mas pino, lingin, ug hamis kini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The raffia palm has the longest leaves of any plant
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card only provides a trivia fact about leaf length; it does not describe the role of leaves (or roots/stems) in obtaining water and nutrients from the soil, which is the focus of G3-L-5.

copy.en:
What plant has the longest leaves?

The raffia palm has the longest leaves of any plant — they can grow up to about 25 meters long!
copy.tl:
Anong halaman ang may pinakamahabang dahon?

Ang raffia palm ang may pinakamahabang dahon sa lahat ng halaman — umaabot ito ng hanggang 25 metro ang haba!
copy.bis:
Unsang tanom ang adunay pinakataas nga dahon?

Ang raffia palm ang adunay pinakataas nga dahon sa tanang tanom — moabot kini og hangtod 25 ka metros ang gitas-on!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: rises above the water on a tall stem
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a stem but only describes the flower's appearance and position above water; it does not teach the stem's role in getting water and nutrients from the soil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The lotus flower is big, usually pink or white
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a flowering plant but provides no table classifying living things into the named groups, and the format-required table is absent.

copy.en: The lotus flower is big, usually pink or white, and rises above the water on a tall stem.
copy.tl: Ang bulaklak ng lotus ay malaki at karaniwang rosas o puti, at tumataas ito sa ibabaw ng tubig sa mahabang tangkay.
copy.bis: Ang bulak sa lotus dako ug kasagaran rosas o puti, ug motungha kini sa ibabaw sa tubig nga naa sa taas nga tangkay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Loudness is just how loud it sounds, while pitch is how high or low the sound is.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card distinguishes loudness and pitch but does not use the scientific wave-property terms (amplitude, frequency, wavelength, velocity) or describe wave properties. It is only topically related to sound.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Loudness is just how loud it sounds, while pitch is how high or low the sound is.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred; it only contrasts two perceptual qualities of sound. No support for the competency's action.

copy.en:
Are loudness and pitch the exact same thing?

No! Loudness is just how loud it sounds, while pitch is how high or low the sound is.
copy.tl:
Magkapareho ba ang lakas at tono ng tunog?

Hindi! Ang lakas ay kung gaano kalakas marinig, habang ang tono ay kung gaano katinis o kalalim nito.
copy.bis:
Pareho ba ang kusog ug ang tono sa tingog?

Dili! Ang kusog mao ang pagkakusog madungog, samtang ang tono mao ang pagka-habog o pagka-halawom niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The big bone at the front of your lower leg, just below the knee, is called the tibia.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card only names the tibia and its location. It does not describe how the skeletal system works (e.g., support, movement, protection, or how bones function together). Naming a single bone is background knowledge, not direct instruction for the competency.

copy.en:
What's the shin bone called?

The big bone at the front of your lower leg, just below the knee, is called the tibia.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tawag sa buto ng binti?

Ang malaking buto sa harap ng binti, sa ibaba ng tuhod, ay tinatawag na tibia.
copy.bis:
Unsay tawag sa bukog sa batiis?

Ang dako nga bukog sa atubangan sa batiis, ubos sa tuhod, gitawag og tibia.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The shore of the Dead Sea is the lowest land on Earth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card names a natural landform/body of water, but it is not a local Philippine example and does not describe how the landform influences living or non-living components of the environment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The shore of the Dead Sea is the lowest land on Earth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify what proportion of the Earth's surface is covered with water as opposed to land
assignedReviews.reason: The card concerns a specific low-lying land location, not the proportion of Earth's surface covered by water versus land, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: The shore of the Dead Sea is the lowest land on Earth, sitting about 430 meters below sea level!
copy.tl: Ang baybayin ng Dead Sea ang pinakamababang lupa sa Earth, na nasa 430 metro sa ilalim ng antas ng dagat!
copy.bis: Ang baybayon sa Dead Sea mao ang pinakaubos nga yuta sa Earth, nga naa sa 430 metros ubos sa lebel sa dagat!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists found water ice inside permanently shadowed craters at the Moon's poles.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a specific fact about the Moon (water ice at its poles) but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, nor does it identify the Moon among major celestial objects, their main features, or general composition in the context of the solar system. The content is only tangentially related to the competency's broad topic.

copy.en:
Is there water on the Moon?

Yes! Scientists found water ice inside permanently shadowed craters at the Moon's poles. In 2009, NASA's LCROSS mission crashed into one and detected water vapour in the dust!
copy.tl:
May tubig ba sa Moon?

Oo! Nakakita ang mga siyentipiko ng water ice sa permanently shadowed craters sa mga polo ng Moon. Noong 2009, nagbangga ang LCROSS mission ng NASA at nakakita ng water vapour sa alikabok!
copy.bis:
May tubig ba sa Moon?

Oo! Nakakaplag ang mga syentipiko og water ice sa permanently shadowed craters sa mga poste sa Moon. Niadtong 2009 mibangga ang LCROSS mission sa NASA ug nakakaplag og water vapour sa abug!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Asthma tightens and swells the tiny tubes in the lungs, making breathing hard.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions lungs and breathing but does not identify the respiratory system parts (nose, windpipe, lungs) from pictures/diagrams or describe how they normally work. It focuses on asthma as a condition, not on the required anatomy or function.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Asthma tightens and swells the tiny tubes in the lungs, making breathing hard.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a breathing difficulty caused by asthma, not how the respiratory system works in simple terms. It does not explain the functioning of the respiratory system as required by the competency.

copy.en:
Why is it hard to breathe with asthma?

Asthma tightens and swells the tiny tubes in the lungs, making breathing hard. Dust, cold, or smoke can trigger it — many Filipino kids use an inhaler to breathe easily again.
copy.tl:
Bakit mahirap huminga kapag may hika?

Sumisikip at namamaga ang maliliit na tubo sa baga, kaya nahihirapang huminga. Pwede itong pukawin ng alikabok, lamig, o usok — maraming batang Pinoy ang may inhaler para makahinga nang maayos.
copy.bis:
Nganong lisod moginhawa kon adunay hika?

Mosikip ug mohubag ang gagmayng tubo sa baga, mao nga maglisod moginhawa. Mahimo kining ma-trigger sa abog, bugnaw, o aso — daghang batang Pilipino ang naggamit og inhaler aron makaginhawa og maayo pag-usab.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You have two lungs, but the left one is a bit smaller to leave room for your heart — together they work as you breathe.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions lungs and breathing but does not identify the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) from pictures/diagrams nor describe how they work. It only gives a fact about lung size relative to the heart.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You have two lungs, but the left one is a bit smaller to leave room for your heart — together they work as you breathe.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on the respiratory system (lungs, breathing) but does not describe how the respiratory system works in simple terms, nor does it cover the other body systems listed. It is only tangentially related.

copy.en:
Are your two lungs the same size?

Not quite! You have two lungs, but the left one is a bit smaller to leave room for your heart — together they work as you breathe.
copy.tl:
Magkasing-laki ba ang dalawa mong baga?

Hindi eksakto! May dalawa tayong baga, pero mas maliit nang kaunti ang kaliwa dahil kailangan ng puwang para sa puso — magkasama silang tumutulong sa paghinga.
copy.bis:
Managsama ba ug kadako ang imong duha ka baga?

Dili gyud parehas! Aduna kitay duha ka baga, apan gamay og gamay ang wala aron adunay luna para sa kasingkasing — magtinabangay sila sa paghinga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most fish use gills to get oxygen from water, but some, like the lungfish, actually have lungs or lung-like organs!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses gills and lungs in fish, not the human respiratory system parts (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work as required by G5-L-2. It shares the respiratory topic but does not directly support identifying or describing the specified human parts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most fish use gills to get oxygen from water, but some, like the lungfish, actually have lungs or lung-like organs!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions gills as a body part used for breathing, but G3-L-4 focuses on outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings and their role in movement and gathering food. Gills are not among the listed examples and the card does not address movement or food gathering.

copy.en:
Do all fish breathe with gills only?

Most fish use gills to get oxygen from water, but some, like the lungfish, actually have lungs or lung-like organs!
copy.tl:
Lahat ba ng isda ay may gills lang?

Karamihan sa isda ay may gills para makakuha ng oxygen mula sa tubig, pero ang ilan, tulad ng lungfish, ay may lungs o katulad na organo!
copy.bis:
Tanan ba nga isda naay gills ra?

Kadaghanan sa isda naay gills aron makakuha og oxygen gikan sa tubig, apan ang uban, sama sa lungfish, naay lungs o susama nga organo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ribs in your chest form a cage that protects your lungs.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single protective function of ribs for lungs. It does not describe how any of the listed body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work—no mechanism, process, or system function is explained. It only mentions a body part and its protective role, which is background knowledge rather than direct instruction for the competency.

copy.en: The ribs in your chest form a cage that protects your lungs.
copy.tl: Ang mga tadyang sa iyong dibdib ay parang hawla na nagpoprotekta sa iyong baga.
copy.bis: Ang mga gusok sa imong dughan nahimong hawla nga manalipod sa imong baga.
